speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your long history of productive cough and recurrent bronchitis despite being a non-smoker, have you ever noticed your lungs producing a "waterfall" sound when you cough, or have you ever seen your doctor mention a "hydroma" on your chest X-rays? Additionally, do you have a history of tuberculosis or silicosis?

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Sputum_Culture: Heavy growth of non-specific bacteria, no TB or fungal growth; Chest_X-ray: Irregular opacities in the right middle lobe and diffuse airway thickening.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The combination of a chronic, productive cough with copious purulent sputum, recurrent exacerbations requiring antibiotics in a non-smoker, and the specific query about "hydromas" (bronchial cysts) strongly points to this structural lung disease rather than simple chronic bronchitis or tuberculosis.
